author: cmungall
body: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q09137/entry note this is annotated as both a kinase and reducatase.. the reductase is propagated to other species (not by PAINT, but by uniprot homology propagation and then rhea/ec.2 go mapping propagation) Molecular Function [[hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA reductase (NADPH)] kinase activity](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0047322)Source:UniProtKB-EC This comes from an EC/RHEA manual annotation on the same protein: This is the paper https://europepmc.org/article/MED/2369897 gpt-5 sycophantic but I believe correct reply: You're quite observant — it *is* unusual to think of **PRKAA2** as both a reductase and a kinase. Let me clarify what’s actually going on in that 1990 paper (PMID: 2369897). ### What's Going On in the Paper? That classic study by Clarke and Hardie, titled *“Regulation of HMG‑CoA reductase: identification of the site phosphorylated by the AMP‑activated protein kinase…”* (EMBO J. Aug 1990), demonstrates that: * **AMP‑activated protein kinase (AMPK)** — for which **PRKAA2** serves as the **α2 catalytic subunit** — **phosphorylates** and thereby **inactivates** HMG‑CoA **reductase**, a key enzyme in cholesterol synthesis ([[PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2369897/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][1], [[Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRKAA2?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2]). * The key wording: AMPK is a **kinase** that acts *upon* HMG‑CoA reductase. It does **not** mean AMPK *is* a reductase. ### So, Is PRKAA2 Both a Reductase and a Kinase? **No** — PRKAA2 is *not* a reductase. It’s strictly a **serine/threonine protein kinase**, specifically the catalytic alpha-2 subunit of AMPK. It functions by **phosphorylating** (i.e., modifying) other enzymes — such as HMG-CoA reductase — **to regulate their activity** ([[PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5722193/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][3]). This could be confusing because one of the substrates it targets is named "HMG-CoA reductase" — but PRKAA2 is the kinase *that acts on* the reductase, **not** itself a reductase. ### Summary * **PRKAA2** = Protein Kinase (part of AMPK complex), functions by **phosphorylation**. * The **1990 paper** shows that this kinase phosphorylates **HMG-CoA reductase**, inactivating it. * There's no evidence or suggestion in that paper that PRKAA2 *is* a reductase. Let me know if you'd like help unpacking more of that paper or related AMPK literature! [1]: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/2369897/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "Regulation of HMG-CoA reductase: identification of the site ..." [2]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PRKAA2?utm_source=chatgpt.com "PRKAA2" [3]: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5722193/?utm_source=chatgpt.com "AMP-activated protein kinase: a target for drugs both ..."
title: PRKAA2 rat wrongly annotated to a reductase and false annotation propagated to other species
